item.title: Women's group Lioness wins lawsuit for air conditioning in Texas prisons
item.description: A group of formerly incarcerated women, united in the nonprofit Lioness Justice Impacted Women's Alliance, has won a lawsuit against the Texas Department of Criminal Justice alongside two other organizations. A federal judge ruled that the state must equip all prisons with air conditioning by the end of 2029. Currently, only 37 percent of approximately 88,697 incarcerated people have access...

item.title: Orphaned hippo Bumpy gets second chance at Sheldrick Wildlife Trust
item.description: On May 2, 2026, the Kenya Wildlife Service received a report of an orphaned hippo in Naivasha, in the Great Rift Valley. The newborn hippo lay beside the body of his mother, who had likely died while defending her calf. After a difficult water rescue operation, the animal, later named Bumpy, was brought to Nairobi and handed over to the...

item.title: Ellinikon Park becomes Europe's largest coastal park
item.description: On the grounds of Athens' former airport in the southern suburbs, The Ellinikon Park is rising: two million square meters of green space that will become Europe's largest coastal urban park (200 hectares). The park is designed to actively lower ambient temperature, processes 100 percent of its own rainwater on-site, and maintains more than 520 plant species through sensor-controlled irrigation....

item.title: 18-year-old Bronx teen sponsors schoolchildren in Ghana
item.description: Max Owobu, an 18-year-old student from the Bronx, founded the Yenko Foundation, a nonprofit organization that finances schooling for children in Ghana. Owobu, whose father grew up in Ghana, has spent summers in the country since age fifteen and witnessed peers working instead of attending school. Using his own allowance, he first paid for the schooling of one child, Matthew,...

item.title: Clay tablet with world's oldest peace treaty discovered
item.description: Archaeologists have found a clay tablet in Turkey containing a fragment of the Treaty of Kadesh, the oldest known peace treaty in the world. The tablet, featuring articles 12 through 20, was excavated last year at the Hittite royal palace in Buyukkale, in the ancient Hittite capital Hattusa. Around 1300 BC, the armies of Pharaoh Ramses II and Hittite King...

item.title: Vietnam protects last habitat of Delacour's langur
item.description: Vietnam has established a specially protected nature reserve for the Delacour's langur, one of the world's most endangered primates. Of this species, named after the French biologist who discovered it, only around 17 populations remain, totalling approximately 250 animals. item.title: French farmers grow papayas and bananas thanks to warming
item.description: In the Var department in southern France, near Toulon, farmers are capitalizing on the warming climate to cultivate tropical fruit. Dominique Berdin grows around 20 different tropical fruits in her greenhouse in Ollioules, including papaya, passion fruit and pineapple, without pesticides. item.title: Ethical fashion brand Yes Friends secures investment from Deborah Meaden
item.description: Bristol-based clothing brand Yes Friends proves that affordable fashion can be ethical. Founded in 2021 with a sustainable T-shirt priced at £7.99, the company has expanded to include underwear and corduroy jackets, with a focus on living wages and low-impact production. Through a tipping scheme, customers can donate money to textile workers; this has already raised over £56,000. Founder Sam...

item.title: Archaeologists rescue 30,000 treasures from Deir ez-Zor Museum before ISIS
item.description: A new study reveals how archaeologists risked their lives to save approximately 30,000 'priceless' artifacts from the Deir ez-Zor Museum in Syria, just before the city threatened to fall into ISIS hands in 2014 and 2015. Study author Maamoun Abdulkarim, then head of Syria's Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums, led the operation. The museum was connected to the military airfield...

item.title: Researchers Find Scents That Keep Honeybees Away From Pesticides
item.description: Researchers at the University of California, Riverside have identified chemical compounds that can safely deter honeybees from pesticide-treated crops. Biologist Anandasankar Ray and entomologist Boris Baer developed a machine-learning model trained on chemical structures and behavioral data from bees and fruit flies to find scents that repel bees. item.title: New York City recovers $131 million from DoorDash for delivery workers
item.description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) has reached a settlement of $131.5 million with DoorDash for violating local delivery worker laws. More than 260,000 workers were underpaid, with some receiving no payment at all or being paid late. Over $115 million will go directly to delivery workers, plus $16 million in fines and costs. item.description: Phil Knight, co-founder of Nike, has made a $1 billion gift to his alma mater, the University of Oregon, together with his wife Penny. According to the New York Times, this is the largest single donation ever made to an American public university. item.description: In Raleigh, North Carolina, Nick Blanchard and Kelly Forbes organized a children's book drive to honor the late music legend and philanthropist Dolly Parton. item.description: These days show that caring for animals and nature leads somewhere, from the savanna to the city. item.title: Orphaned rhino Tytan and zebra Notty inseparable after losing their mothers
item.description: At the Sheldrick Wildlife Trust in Nairobi, which has been caring for injured and orphaned animals in East Africa since 1977, a special bond formed between two young animals. Black rhino Tytan lost his mother when he was eight months old after she fell from a cliff. A week later, zebra Notty was brought to the same sanctuary after her...

item.title: Ghana cuckoo-shrike resurfaces in Ivory Coast after 13 years
item.description: Researchers Paulo Ditzel and Stephanie Bartlett of the International Bird Conservation Partnership (IBCP) have spotted the Ghana cuckoo-shrike (Lobotos lobatus) again, in Taï National Park in Côte d'Ivoire. The last confirmed sighting of this striking orange-yellow-black bird dated from 2013, in the Atewa forest in Ghana. During a bird count, Ditzel spotted the bird among a group of other species.

item.title: Nonprofit Rise Up trains formerly incarcerated men as machinists
item.description: In a converted workshop in Southeast San Diego, the nonprofit Rise Up Industries teaches men who spent decades in prison the trade of machinist. The program combines paid apprenticeships with therapy and case management. The workshop fulfills orders for aerospace, medical equipment, auto parts, and fishing lures, among others. According to Rise Up, only 3% of graduates reoffend, compared to...

item.description: Rangers at Yellowstone National Park have removed more than 20,100 pieces of trash, 5,000 stones and branches, and 280 visitor hats from the park's geothermal areas this year, including Old Faithful and Midway Geyser Basin. item.title: World record: largest beaver dam hidden in Wood Buffalo National Park
item.description: In Canada's Wood Buffalo National Park, an area as large as Switzerland, lies the world's largest beaver dam. The dam was only discovered in 2007 through satellite imagery by landscape ecologist Jean Thie; park managers had no knowledge of it until then. item.title: Reading for pleasure protects the brain against dementia
item.description: A new review by researchers from Cambridge University shows that reading for pleasure, whether from an old paperback or an e-reader, is linked to better memory and attention, fewer mental health problems, and a significantly lower risk of dementia. These findings apply to all age groups: you don't need to have been an avid reader as a child to benefit...

item.title: Ethiopians plant millions of trees via Green Legacy Initiative
item.description: Ethiopia lost around 560,000 hectares of forest between 2000 and 2025 to agriculture, logging and charcoal production. In 2019, the government launched the Green Legacy Initiative, which saw citizens planting trees on a massive scale. Yitebitu Moges of UNEP's REDD+ programme says that even if only half the trees survive, there are already gains for moisture, soil and carbon storage....

item.title: Livestream captures wildlife at remote waterhole in Watarrka
item.description: At Australia's Watarrka National Park, a camouflaged camera livestreams a remote desert waterhole to the world. Positioned 1.2 miles from the nearest parking area, the camera captures dingoes, wallabies, frogs, feral cats and even a wedge-tailed eagle as they come to drink. item.title: New wild cat species tilcayo discovered in Bolivia
item.description: A new wild cat species has been confirmed in the Yungas cloud forest in Bolivia: the tilcayo, scientifically named Leopardus tilcayo. For years, the spotted animal was regarded as an ordinary ocelot, but local communities had always called it by a different name. item.title: South Korea recycles 97 percent of all food waste
item.description: In Seoul, Seunghwan Hong tosses his food scraps into a smart waste bin: he taps his card, the bin weighs the waste and he pays by weight.
